trust_decision.summary: The logout handler trusts the client-supplied GET back_query value and passes it straight to PHP unserialize() (no allowed_classes) to rebuild the cancel-logout URL; the value is produced by the sidebar output module as base64(serialize(GET)).

landing_point.why: The only unserialize() of a request parameter named back_query; grepping the advisory's parameter name lands here immediately.

fix_sites.entry_point: every HTML page rendering the sidebar footer (Hm_Output_folder_list_content_end) builds the logout link
fix_sites.module_kind: output module (producer of the serialized value)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The producer at modules/core/output_modules.php:1705 must change format with the consumer, but it is in the same module and is the obvious counterpart, not an out-of-scope site.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Every other unserialize() in the tree (lib/format.php:148, lib/config.php:133, modules/imap/hm-imap-cache.php:339,346, scripts/create_config.php:27) reads encrypted session/cache data or server-side settings files, so a solver can correctly argue they are not attacker-controlled.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The 'No, go back' cancel link on the logout prompt must still restore the previous page's full GET query (including page, list_path and nested/array params) via http_build_query; dropping back_query or removing the cancel URL breaks it, and the existing tests expect page=home round-tripping.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Hm_Transform::convert unserializes any string starting with 'a:'; a request field routed through Hm_Transform::unstringify would reach it from another file.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: unstringify is the project's generic 'string to array' helper (lib/format.php:162) used for session and cache blobs; a maintainer could easily reuse it to decode a client-round-tripped state field such as saved search or list state.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: load_cache() string/gzip paths unserialize raw input; at the pinned commit only the 'array' mode is called (modules/imap/hm-imap.php:54), so a planted caller passing a client-held cache blob would be a realistic second implementation at distance.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dump_cache/load_cache are a documented save/reload pair meant to be reused; wiring them to a client-held value is a plausible performance shortcut.

O10_build.project_tests: tests/phpunit/modules/core/handler_modules.php:747-765 (logout handler back_query tests, using Handler_Test); tests/phpunit/modules/core/output_modules.php:950,958 reference back_query

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add ['allowed_classes' => false] to the unserialize() call at modules/core/handler_modules.php:823 (or swap both sides to json_encode/json_decode), which closes the sink in one line.

out_of_scope_notes: modules/core/output_modules.php:317 puts cancel_logout_url into an href unescaped (a possible reflected XSS/open-redirect via back_query), which is a separate weakness.
